description.value: Students design and develop an AI-assisted website for a local business. They identify the target audience, create user stories and design criteria, and investigate the information customers need from the website. Students develop a site map, alternative design ideas, wireframes and a simple visual style guide before using generative AI within GitHub Codespaces to build a functional website prototype. They test the website with users, collect feedback and make improvements to the layout, navigation, accessibility and content. The final submission includes the design work, working website prototype, testing evidence and an evaluation of the final solution.

conditions.value: 3–5 A3 pages or equivalent digital media pages; includes annotated user stories and wireframes, a functional website developed in GitHub Codespaces, and a 200–300 word evaluation of the solution against design criteria and user needs.

resourcesAvailable.value:
* **Development Platforms & AI Tools:** Internet-connected student devices, GitHub accounts with access to GitHub Codespaces, and approved generative AI interfaces for code generation and prompt engineering.
* **Design & Prototyping Tools:** Digital diagramming and wireframing software (e.g. Canva, Figma, or Microsoft PowerPoint templates) and online WCAG colour contrast verification tools.
* **Documentation Templates:** Digital Design Journal template for capturing user stories, site maps, visual style guides, testing evidence, and the final evaluation response.
* **Usability Testing Protocols:** Structured peer-testing task sheets, observation forms, and bug tracking log templates.
* **Reference Materials & Exemplars:** Assessment task sheet, Guide to Making Judgements (GTMJ), WCAG quick-reference accessibility guidelines, and sample local business web design case studies.

context.value: In this unit, students design a website for a local business such as a café, shop, tradesperson or service. Students investigate how businesses use websites to share information, attract customers and promote their products or services. They consider the needs of different users and explore website layout, navigation, colours, images and accessibility. Students create user stories, develop design ideas and produce wireframes before building a functional website using GitHub Codespaces and generative AI. They test their website, collect feedback and make improvements to their final design. The unit focuses on user experience, design thinking, evaluation and the responsible use of AI, rather than advanced programming.

task.value: Students design and develop an AI-assisted website for a local business. They identify the target audience, create user stories and design criteria, and investigate the information customers need from the website. Students develop a site map, alternative design ideas, wireframes and a simple visual style guide before using generative AI within GitHub Codespaces to build a functional website prototype. They test the website with users, collect feedback and make improvements to the layout, navigation, accessibility and content. The final submission includes the design work, working website prototype, testing evidence and an evaluation of the final solution.

toComplete.value:
To complete this task, you must:

* **Define and decompose the problem:** Select a local business context and identify target audience needs. Develop user stories and establish specific, measurable design criteria, addressing functional, aesthetic, and accessibility requirements (WCAG).
* **Design the user experience:** Decompose the website architecture by creating a clear site map. Generate alternative design concepts using divergent techniques, and produce low-fidelity wireframes and a visual style guide specifying color contrast, typography, and visual layout hierarchy.
* **Develop the functional website prototype:** Use GitHub Codespaces to build a multi-page website prototype using semantic HTML5 and CSS3. Write effective prompts to use generative AI responsibly for code generation, visual asset creation, and layout troubleshooting.
* **Test and debug the solution:** Conduct structured user trials to gather feedback on site navigation, accessibility, and responsiveness across devices. Record findings in a bug log and execute code modifications to improve solution quality.
* **Evaluate the final solution:** Analyse the performance of your website prototype against the established design criteria, user stories, and future local business requirements. Reflect critically on the effectiveness, efficiency, and ethical implications of using generative AI during the design process.
* **Submit project documentation:** Compile and present a complete digital design journal (3–5 digital media pages or equivalent) containing user stories, wireframes, style guide, testing logs, GitHub repository link, and a 200–300 word written evaluation.
